overall: Thursday (June 25) in Atlanta looks like a classic late-June warm day — mostly sunny skies, light south winds of 0-5 mph, and a high near 89°F per NWS. No tropical or severe weather concerns affect the area; the only active alerts are patchy dense fog in far north Georgia (clearing by 10 AM) and minor river flooding on the Satilla River in distant south Georgia, neither of which influences Atlanta's afternoon high.
forecast_obs_notes: Most models are well-clustered in the upper 80s to near 90°F: ECMWF projects 88.1°F, HRRR 89.5°F, NBM 87.0°F, and Weather.com 87.3°F. The notable outlier is GFS at 77.4°F, which is a meaningful departure from the consensus and is the primary source of downside spread in the ensemble; the weight of evidence strongly favors the 87-90°F cluster over the GFS cooler solution.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model places the expected TMAX at 87.2°F, with the even-bucket distribution concentrating mass on 90-91°F (51.6%) and 88-89°F (49.5%), pointing to a most-likely range of roughly 88-91°F. The even-bucket set earns Tier 2 confidence (expected accuracy ~52%) with a modest 2-point gap between top buckets, while the odd-bucket set shows poor signal and should be avoided. Mostly sunny conditions, seasonally warm air advection from the south, and strong multi-model agreement (excluding GFS) support a best estimate near 88°F, with the primary risk being GFS verifying — which would push the high well below 85°F.
